CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING AGENDA
  “We are a vibrant, livable, and inclusive community dedicated to quality services,
  safety, financial strength, sustainability, preservation, and progress
  with equal representation for our community.”

City Council Chamber  Tuesday
225 Second Street  June 25, 2024
Claremont, CA 91711
  6:30 PM

  COUNCILMEMBERS

  SAL MEDINA
  MAYOR

  JED LEANO  ED REECE  COREY CALAYCAY  JENNIFER STARK

Meetings are open to the public for in-person attendance. The meeting will be live streamed via Zoom,
technology permitting. Members of the public will not be able to provide public comment via Zoom. To
watch the meeting via Zoom, use the following link: https://zoom.us/j/256208090. To listen via telephone
dial (213)338-8477, Webinar ID: 256 208 090. The recorded meeting will be uploaded to the City
website and archived.

  OPTIONS FOR PUBLIC COMMENT

Public comment may be provided by one of the following methods. Each speaker will be given up to
three (3) minutes to provide their comment.

  IN-PERSON LIVE COMMENTS

When the item you wish to speak to is announced, please proceed to the speaker’s podium one by one.

  E-MAIL/MAIL

Written comments sent to the City Clerk’s office will be distributed to the City Council and imaged into
the record of the meeting. Email: sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us, jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. Mail:
PO Box 880, Claremont, CA 91711. Written comments submitted after publication of the agenda will be
made available in the document archive system on the City website as soon as possible -
www.ci.claremont.ca.us.

  For assistance, comments, or more information please contact the City Clerk’s Office:
  (909) 399-5461 or (909) 399-5463.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL

Council Item
1.  APPOINTMENT OF MEMBER TO THE SUSTAINABILITY COMMITTEE
  Recommendation:  The City Council Ad Hoc Nominating Committee recommends the City
  Council appoint Emily Condon to the Sustainability Committee, for a term to
  expire on January 31, 2028.

Council Assignment Reports
City Councilmembers may serve as representatives on regional organizations. This time is
allocated for reports about their activities. For information about the Council's local,
intergovernmental  and  regional  appointments  please  visit  the  City website :
www.ci.claremont.ca.us/government/city-council/city-council-assignments-and-appointments.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

PUBLIC COMMENT
The Council has set aside this time for persons who wish to comment on items that are not listed
on the agenda, but are within the jurisdiction of the City Council. Members of the public will have
the opportunity to address the City Council regarding all items on the agenda at the time the
Council considers those items.
 Page 3  City Council Agenda  June 25, 2024

General public comment will be taken for 30 minutes and will resume later in the meeting if there
are speakers who did not get an opportunity to speak because of the 30-minute time limit.

The Brown Act prohibits the City Council from taking action on oral requests relating to items that
are not on the agenda. The Council may engage in a brief discussion, refer the matter to staff,
and/or schedule requests for consideration at a subsequent meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR
All matters listed on the Consent Calendar are considered routine. The City Council may act on
these items by one motion following public comment. Only Councilmembers may pull an item from
the Consent Calendar for discussion, reading of resolutions and ordinances will be waived.
2.  RESIGNATION OF SUSTAINABILITY COMMITTEE MEMBER HELEN MEIER
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council accept with regret the resignation of
  Helen Meier from the Sustainability Committee.
  Attachment(s):  Resignation of Sustainability Committee Member Helen Meier

3.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE CITY WARRANT REGISTER
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID, dated June 20, 2024.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Approving City Warrant Register Dated June 20, 2024

4.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 11, 2024 (SPECIAL AND REGULAR)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council approve the special and regular City
  Council meeting minutes of June 11, 2024.
  Attachment(s):  Draft Special Meeting Minutes of June 11, 2024
  Draft Regular Meeting Minutes of June 11, 2024
 Page 4  City Council Agenda  June 25, 2024

5.  MEMORANDA OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF CLAREMONT AND
  VARIOUS EMPLOYEE ASSOCIATIONS AND A RESOLUTION FOR UNREPRESENTED
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES IMPLEMENTING WAGES, HOURS, AND TERMS AND
  CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR FISCAL YEARS 2024-25, 2025-26, AND 2026-27
  (FUNDING SOURCE: VARIOUS CITY OPERATING FUNDS)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council:
  A. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  IMPLEMENT WAGES, HOURS, AND TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027; and
  B. Adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, SETTING FORTH THE HOURS, WAGES, AND
  WORKING  CONDITIONS  FOR  CERTAIN  UNREPRESENTED
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2027.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Approving MOUs
  Unrepresented Management Resolution

  PART-TIME JOB CLASSIFICATIONS FOR FISCAL YEARS 2024-25, 2025-26, AND 2026-27
  (FUNDING SOURCE: VARIOUS FUNDS)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING
  REVISED SALARY SCHEDULES FOR PART-TIME JOB CLASSIFICATIONS
  FOR FISCAL YEARS 2024-25, 2025-26, AND 2026-27.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Revised Salary Schedule for Part-Time

7.  PROPOSED REVISIONS TO THE COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATION  GRANT
  ALLOCATION POLICY (FUNDING SOURCE: AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council approve the revisions to the Community
  Based Organization Grant Allocation Policy.
  Attachment(s):  Revised CBO Grant Allocation Policy (Draft)
  2025 CBO Grant Application Form
  2025 CBO Ad Hoc Evaluation Rubric
 Page 5  City Council Agenda  June 25, 2024

8.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH THE CLAREMONT CHAMBER
  OF COMMERCE FOR VISITOR CENTER SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE: AMERICAN
  RESCUE PLAN ACT FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into a
  two-year agreement with the Chamber of Commerce in the amount of
  $60,000 per year ($120,000 total) to provide visitor center services on behalf
  of the City for a term starting on July 1, 2024.
9.  AUTHORIZATION TO AMEND THE EXISTING PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH CPS HR CONSULTING FOR DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION PROGRAMMING
  AND CONSULTING SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to amend the
  existing professional services agreement with CPS HR Consulting to increase
  compensation by $50,000 for a total not-to-exceed amount of $162,150, and
  to extend the contract term to June 30, 2026.
10. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH COMPUMERIC ENGINEERING,
  INC. FOR THE PURCHASE OF BEAR-RESISTANT TRASH RECEPTACLES FOR THE
  CLAREMONT HILLS WILDERNESS PARK (FUNDING SOURCE: RIVERS AND MOUNTAINS
  CONSERVANCY GRANT)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a
  purchase agreement with Compumeric Engineering, Inc. for the purchase of
  thirty bear-resistant trash receptacles in the amount of $58,127.71 for the
  Claremont Hills Wilderness Park.
  Attachment(s):  BearSaver Quote

11. AWARD OF CONTRACT TO EEC ENVIRONMENTAL FOR FATS, OILS, AND GREASE
  (FOG) PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AND INSPECTION SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE:
  SEWER FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute a
  professional services agreement with EEC Environmental in an amount not to
  exceed $75,000 annually for three years, with two optional one-year
  extensions, for a total amount not to exceed $375,000 for FOG Program
  Management and Inspection Services.
 Page 6  City Council Agenda  June 25, 2024

12. AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH SUN RIDGE SYSTEMS, INC.,
  FOR THE PURCHASE OF A RECORD INFORMATION MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
  COMPUTER AIDED DISPATCH AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE (CAD/RMS)
  FOR THE POLICE DEPARTMENT (FUNDING SOURCE: AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT
  FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement for $499,734 to
  purchase, implement, and provide one year of support for the Sun Ridge
  Systems, Inc., Record Information Management System (RIMS) Computer
  Aided Dispatch and Records Management System, including an additional
  Mobile Data Communication module;
  B. Appropriate $499,734 from the American Rescue Plan Act Fund to fully
  fund the purchase, implementation, and one year of support of the RIMS
  system; and
  C. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a one-year agreement in the
  amount of $87,461.57 for continued Pulsiam CAD/RMS/MDC maintenance
  and support during the transition.
13. AUTHORIZATION TO AMEND THE AGREEMENT WITH KOA CORPORATION FOR THE
  MOUNTAIN AVENUE CORRIDOR (BASE LINE ROAD TO BONITA AVENUE) COMPLETE
  STREETS IMPROVEMENTS DESIGN (FUNDING SOURCE: STATE GAS TAX FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to execute an amendment to the agreement
  with KOA Corporation for the design of the Mountain Avenue Corridor (Base
  Line Road to Bonita Avenue) Complete Streets Project in the amount of
  $396,021, increasing the total contract amount to $827,319; and
  B. Find this item is exempt from environmental review under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
14. AUTHORIZATION TO AMEND THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH KOA
  CORPORATION FOR THE PREPARATION OF A LOCAL ROAD SAFETY PLAN (FUNDING
  SOURCE: PROPOSITION C)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute an
  amendment to the professional services agreement with KOA Corporation for
  the outreach efforts being conducted for the preparation of a Local Road
  Safety Plan in the amount of $55,839, for a total not-to-exceed contract
  amount of $172,140.
15. USER FEE RATE INCREASE OF 3.90 PERCENT BASED UPON THE CONSUMER PRICE
  INDEX (CPI) FROM APRIL 2023 TO APRIL 2024 TO THE CITYWIDE USER FEE
  SCHEDULE, EFFECTIVE JULY 1, 2024 (FUNDING SOURCE: VARIOUS FUNDS)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council receive and file the 2024 Citywide User
  Fee Schedule, effective July 1, 2024.
  Attachment(s):  Proposed Citywide User Fee Schedule FY 2024
  Fully Burdened Hourly Rates
 Page 7  City Council Agenda  June 25, 2024
